name: Bhakti movement
title: The story of the Bhakti movement

text: Long ago in India, priests called Brahmins guarded the holy books, which were written in Sanskrit.
An old holy book, the Bhagavad Gita, already spoke of loving devotion to the god Krishna.
src: Religious authority, however, still rested largely with Brahmin priests and scholars, who performed the rites and guarded the Sanskrit scriptures
The Bhagavad Gita, probably composed in the last centuries BCE, presents devotion to Krishna as a path to liberation

text: More than 1,400 years ago, poet-saints in south India walked from temple to temple, singing to their gods.
They sang in Tamil, the language people spoke, not in Sanskrit.
src: Beginning among Tamil poet-saints in the 6th to 9th centuries / wandering poet-saints who went from temple to temple singing of the god who dwelt in each
they sang in Tamil, not Sanskrit, to any who would listen / The saints spoke and sang in the languages of ordinary people

text: Bhakti means loving devotion to a god.
The saints taught that loving a god such as Krishna, Rama or Shiva was the surest way to be set free.
src: came to mean loving devotion to a god
loving devotion to a personal god is the surest path to liberation / above all Krishna and Rama, or Shiva

text: The saints came from every part of society, from weavers and potters to a princess.
Tradition says the princess Mirabai sang and danced for Krishna, though her husband's family was against it.
src: The poet-saints came from every level of society / Kabir grew up in a family of Muslim weavers / Gora a potter / Mirabai, by contrast, was a Rajput princess
Mirabai, by contrast, was a Rajput princess who, tradition holds, defied her royal in-laws to sing and dance before Krishna

text: Over a thousand years the movement spread across India, and Chaitanya taught people to chant Krishna's names.
The saints taught that caste, the group a person is born into, meant nothing before God, but caste lived on.
src: it spread region by region over a thousand years / spreading the chanting of Krishna's names
The saints taught that caste meant nothing before God, but caste itself survived

text: Rabindranath Tagore put the poems of the saint Kabir into English, and readers far beyond India found them.
The saints' songs are still part of daily life in India, and every year huge crowds of pilgrims walk to Pandharpur.
src: Kabir's poems, in English versions by Rabindranath Tagore and later poets, found readers far beyond India
The songs of the bhakti saints remain part of daily life in India / Each year hundreds of thousands of Varkari pilgrims walk to Pandharpur
